This paper examines the fundamental role of ³He in dilution refrigeration systems, the physical principles underlying its necessity, current supply challenges, and implications for the quantum computing industry. We demonstrate that ³He-based cooling is not merely advantageous but essential for most contemporary quantum computing architectures, with no immediately viable alternatives at comparable performance levels.
